fields.Name: International Cheese Federation: August 2019 Archive
fields.Description: This archive page from the International Cheese Federation features a collection of blog posts and news updates from August 2019. Topics include registration for a judging standards webinar, member success stories, new tariffs impacting US cheese exports to China, details on the Sensory Evaluation Certificate, guidance on food safety exemptions for small dairy processors, environmental monitoring programs, cave management education, and updates on federal dairy margin support programs.

Registration opens for the judging standards webinar 

 

Our September judging standards webinar opens for registration this week. A look at what the session covers and why it matters even if you never step onto a competition floor.

The counter clerk who became the buyer 

 

A member who started slicing wedges behind a retail counter now sets the buying list for three shops. Her route through the credential ladder says something about how careers actually bend.

A new tariff line lands next week 

 

A fresh round of duties on US cheese bound for China takes effect September 1. Here’s what we’re hearing from members who ship, and what to check before the change lands.

A Jura affineur’s one week a year 

 

One of our members flies in from the Jura once a year for a single week of meetings and cave tours — and this year he arrived with more questions about the tariff line than usual.

Yuri Lee 




 


What your nose can’t unlearn 

 

The Sensory Evaluation Certificate asks members to name a flaw, not just notice one — and most candidates find that the naming, not the noticing, is what takes practice.

The paperwork that proves the exemption 

 

Federal food-safety rules exempt many small dairy processors from the full preventive-controls plan, but the exemption isn’t automatic — and members keep asking us to explain how to document it.
